title: Approvals inbox: tab, filters, search and sort are lost after opening a request and pressing Back
body:
## What happens

In the approvals inbox (`/_console/apps/<app>/component/approvals/inbox`), the tab, the status / process / object filters, the search text and the sort order are lost as soon as the reader opens a request and comes back. The inbox always returns to **Pending** with every filter cleared.

Someone working through "All → Withdrawn" or "Submitted by me" has to pick the tab and rebuild the filters after every single request they open.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open any app → Approvals inbox.
2. Switch to the **All** tab and set the status filter to **Withdrawn** (any tab other than Pending, or any filter / search / sort, shows the same thing).
3. Click a row. The console navigates to `/_console/apps/<owning app>/sys_approval_request/record/<areq_id>`.
4. Press the browser's Back button.

## Observed

The inbox shows the **Pending** tab, status / process / object filters back to "All", search empty, sort back to "Newest first".

Measured on the console shipped with `@objectstack/*` 18.6.0 (zh-CN):

| | Before opening the request | After Back |
|---|---|---|
| Selected tab | 全部 (All) | 待我审批 (Pending) |
| Status filter | 已撤回 (Withdrawn) | not shown (Pending tab has none) |
| Rows | 5 | 1 |

## Expected

Back returns to the tab, filters, search and sort the reader left, as object list views already do (their filter / sort / group / search are carried in the URL as `uf__*` parameters and survive Back).

## Cause

`ui/apps/console/src/pages/system/ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx` on `main` keeps all of this in component state only, so it is reset whenever `ApprovalsQueue` remounts:

```tsx
// line 986
const [tab, setTab] = useState<TabKey>('pending');
```

The status / process / object filters, the query and the sort key are `useState` values next to it (see `onTabChange`, line 1764, which resets them all). Nothing is written to the URL or to storage. The page already reads `useSearchParams()` for `?request=`, so carrying `tab`, `status`, `process`, `object`, `q` and `sort` in the query string would be enough.

## Environment

- `@objectstack/*` 18.6.0, console at `/_console`
- Same code on `main` at the time of filing
